title: AtScale query lifecycle (Elasticsearch logs)
description: Inbound Query, Planning, Outbound and Result Processing per AtScale query, from the AtScale query history. Sample code, provided as is, not supported by AtScale. Logs from Elasticsearch.

panels.title: Queries
panels.description: Queries that finished in the selected range (from the AtScale query history).

targets.expr: sum(increase(atscale_query_duration_seconds_count{env=~"$env",query_type=~"$query_type",catalog=~"$catalog",model=~"$model",optimization=~"$optimization",status=~"$status"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Avg duration

panels.title: Why queries missed aggregates and cache
Queries without aggregate or cache, by reason
panels.description: Why queries ran without an aggregate or the cache. Aggregate created by this query: the first run of a new combination of attributes and measures; AtScale created an aggregate while it ran, so the next run can use it. No aggregate created: investigate, for example an exact distinct count that no aggregate holds, or a catalog deployed while the query ran. No warehouse query: answered without a warehouse query (metadata). AtScale system query: AtScale's own queries, for example aggregate builds and statistics. Unclassified: the exporter could not read the aggregates API.

panels.title: Single queries (needs the exporter's query log in Elasticsearch)
Slowest queries
panels.description: One row per query from the exporter's JSON query log, slowest first. Click a Query ID to show its inbound and outbound query text below or its trace in Tempo, or search for it on the Queries page in AtScale Design Center. The other panels work without Elasticsearch. Read from Elasticsearch (data streams logs-atscale.engine / logs-atscale.exporter, fields from the ingest pipelines in deploy/elastic).

targets.query: atscale.event:atscale_query AND atscale.env:${env:lucene} AND atscale.query_type:${query_type:lucene} AND atscale.catalog:${catalog:lucene} AND atscale.model:${model:lucene} AND atscale.optimization:${optimization:lucene} AND atscale.status:${status:lucene}

panels.title: Query text for $query_id
panels.description: The inbound MDX, DAX or SQL that the client sent and the outbound SQL that AtScale sent to the warehouse, for the Query ID field at the top. Click a Query ID in Slowest queries to fill it. Read from the AtScale engine log in Elasticsearch (Engine log filter at the top). Needs a log collector that joins multi-line engine log entries (lines that do not start with a timestamp) into one entry. The engine log contains user names and the filter values of each query. Read from Elasticsearch (data streams logs-atscale.engine / logs-atscale.exporter, fields from the ingest pipelines in deploy/elastic).

targets.query: atscale.query_id:"$query_id" AND atscale.event:(inbound OR outbound) AND ($engine_filter)

panels.title: Warehouse connection queue for $query_id
panels.description: Warehouse queries of the query in the Query ID field, by connection, and the deepest place in the connection queue. 1 means no request waited; a higher place means this query waited behind others. Compare with Outbound wait in Slowest queries. Each warehouse query asks the AtScale connection manager for a connection to the data warehouse. The engine logs the request with its place in line: #1 means first in line, a higher place means the request waited behind others. User queries share the connection with AtScale's own services (statistics, aggregate builds, health checks). Deep queues explain a high Outbound wait. Read from the AtScale engine log in Elasticsearch (Engine log filter at the top); only the time range applies. Read from Elasticsearch (data streams logs-atscale.engine / logs-atscale.exporter, fields from the ingest pipelines in deploy/elastic).

targets.query: atscale.query_id:"$query_id" AND atscale.event:queue AND ($engine_filter) AND atscale.queue_position:>1

panels.title: Aggregate candidates and compression score (needs the AtScale engine log in Elasticsearch)
Aggregate candidates by dataset and grain
panels.description: Compression score = rows in the fact dataset / estimated rows of the proposed aggregate, as the AtScale engine logs it for each aggregate candidate (rule R050). With aggregates.create.threshold.enabled, candidates below aggregates.create.compression.threshold (default 3.0) are not created. Read from the AtScale engine log in Elasticsearch (Engine log filter at the top); the engine log has no catalog or model, so only the time range applies. Below threshold uses the Compression threshold field at the top. Read from Elasticsearch (data streams logs-atscale.engine / logs-atscale.exporter, fields from the ingest pipelines in deploy/elastic).

targets.query: atscale.event:aggregate_candidate AND atscale.score:[$min_score TO $max_score] AND ($engine_filter) AND atscale.score:<$compression_threshold

panels.title: Aggregate suggestions for slow queries
panels.description: Queries that ran at least Min runtime (ms), joined on the query ID with the aggregate candidates the engine proposed for them that are below the Compression threshold. AtScale does not create those. One row per query and fact dataset; UDA (SML) holds the aggregates: block for that fact dataset, at the grain of the query (its attributes), with the base metrics behind its measures; comments name what was left out. Candidates that meet the threshold are in Aggregate candidates per query. Check before you create it: the query's attributes must be coarser than the rejected grain (for example Fiscal Quarter instead of Day), and calculated measures must be replaced by the base metrics they use. Queries that used an aggregate have no candidates and do not appear. Compression score = rows in the fact dataset / estimated rows of the proposed aggregate, as the AtScale engine logs it for each aggregate candidate (rule R050). With aggregates.create.threshold.enabled, candidates below aggregates.create.compression.threshold (default 3.0) are not created. Read from the AtScale engine log in Elasticsearch (Engine log filter at the top); the engine log has no catalog or model, so only the time range applies. panels.title: Warehouse connection queue (needs the AtScale engine log in Elasticsearch)
Deepest place in the warehouse connection queue
panels.description: Highest queue place per interval and connection. 1 means no request waited. Each warehouse query asks the AtScale connection manager for a connection to the data warehouse. The engine logs the request with its place in line: #1 means first in line, a higher place means the request waited behind others. User queries share the connection with AtScale's own services (statistics, aggregate builds, health checks). Deep queues explain a high Outbound wait. Read from the AtScale engine log in Elasticsearch (Engine log filter at the top); only the time range applies.
